what: Input delays are set without -max/-min, so 4.0 ns is also used as the minimum input delay for hold analysis. A 4.0 ns minimum arrival adds 4 ns of artificial hold margin on every input-to-register path (a, b, op, rst_n -> result/flag flops), so hold checks for those paths are optimistic and could hide a real hold violation after CTS (clock insertion delay vs. a short input-to-flop path).
evidence: spec/spec.yaml open_questions: 'assume inputs arrive and outputs leave with 0 ns external delay unless the customer states one'. REQ-014 acceptance requires 'hold WNS >= 0.0 ns, as decided by the real STA tool'. The SDC sets only 'set_input_delay 4.0 ...' with no '-min' value, so the hold-case external arrival is 4.0 ns instead of the spec-assumed 0 ns.
suggested_action: Synthesis owner (Sienna) to split the constraint: keep 'set_input_delay -max 4.0' (or the G1-approved budget) for setup and add 'set_input_delay -min 0.0' on rst_n, a[*], b[*], op[*] so hold is checked against the spec's 0 ns assumption; record the choice in docs/DECISIONS.md. Re-run STA and report input-path hold slack.
